doc.name: Besorah — the Bible in Hebrew, Greek, Aramaic and English
doc.instructions: Read-only access to the whole Bible (Hebrew, Greek, Aramaic, English): read passages, search the text, study a verse word by word, look up Hebrew/Greek words (Strong's, Brown–Driver–Briggs), find every verse a word is in, and follow cross-references, quotations and parallels. Every result carries a url to the page it came from. Texts and data are open: terms and licences at https://besorah.bible/data-licence.txt.

tools.name: get_passage
tools.description: Returns a verse, range or chapter in its original language (Hebrew, Greek or Aramaic) with its English and a link; a range is capped at 80 verses. edition (septuagint, onkelos, pseudo-jonathan, jonathan, hebrew-nt, hebrew, greek) chooses the text. words=true adds, for each verse whose words line up with the Strong's tagging, every word's Strong's number, lemma, meaning and grammatical parsing. Use when the user asks to read or quote a verse, range or chapter.

edition.description: which text, e.g. septuagint, onkelos, pseudo-jonathan, jonathan, hebrew-nt, hebrew or greek

words.description: true adds each word's Strong's number, lemma, meaning and parsing

max_chars.description: optional: cap the answer at about this many characters (lists are shortened and marked truncated; use offset/nextOffset to get the rest)

tools.title: Read a passage

tools.name: get_verse_study
tools.description: Returns one verse, or a range of up to 5, in full: the original and English text; word-by-word Strong's number, lemma and parsing where the words line up with the tagging; and the verse's cross-references, quotations between books, curated parallels, similar wording, questions it asks or answers, songs, scribal marks, Ketiv/Qere and Targum connections. Use when the user wants a thorough look at one verse, or up to five.

edition.description: which text, e.g. septuagint, onkelos, pseudo-jonathan, jonathan, hebrew-nt, hebrew or greek

max_chars.description: optional: cap the answer at about this many characters (lists are shortened and marked truncated; use offset/nextOffset to get the rest)

tools.title: Study a verse

tools.name: search_text
tools.description: Returns the verses that match a search of the text, in Bible order, each with its reference, link and text; 10 per page by default (limit 1-25, and nextOffset continues). English by default; language=hebrew|greek|aramaic searches the original with vowel points and accents ignored. Every word must be in the verse; \"quoted phrase\" matches exact order; a trailing * matches word endings (lov*); English words are matched as written, without stemming. Narrow with book, testament (tanakh|new testament|apocrypha) or edition. Use when the user searches for words or phrases in the text itself.

query.description: the words or "quoted phrase" to find; a trailing * matches word endings (lov*)

language.description: which text is searched: english, hebrew, greek or aramaic

book.description: restrict to one book, e.g. Isaiah

edition.description: which text, e.g. septuagint, onkelos, pseudo-jonathan, jonathan, hebrew-nt, hebrew or greek

limit.description: how many results to return (1-25, default 10)

offset.description: how many results to skip; the previous answer's nextOffset is where its page ended

max_chars.description: optional: cap the answer at about this many characters (lists are shortened and marked truncated; use offset/nextOffset to get the rest)

tools.title: Search the text

tools.name: search_words
tools.description: Finds Hebrew and Greek words (Strong's entries) from an English word, a transliteration ('shalom', 'agape') or the original word. Returns the best matches first (10 by default, up to 25), each with its Strong's id, lemma, definition, occurrence count and link; 'more' says how many further matches exist. Use when the user asks which Hebrew or Greek word lies behind an English word or transliteration.

query.description: an English word, a transliteration (shalom, agape) or the Hebrew or Greek word itself

limit.description: how many results to return (1-25, default 10)

max_chars.description: optional: cap the answer at about this many characters (lists are shortened and marked truncated; use offset/nextOffset to get the rest)

tools.title: Find a Hebrew or Greek word

annotations.title: Find a Hebrew or Greek word

tools.name: get_word
tools.description: Returns one Strong's entry (Hebrew H… or Greek G…): lemma, transliteration, definition, KJV renderings, occurrence count and verses per book. For Hebrew it adds the Brown–Driver–Briggs entry and, for a name, how it is built from its parts; it also gives the Septuagint renderings of a Hebrew word, or the Hebrew words a Greek word renders. Use when the user asks what a Hebrew or Greek word means, given its Strong's number.

max_chars.description: optional: cap the answer at about this many characters (lists are shortened and marked truncated; use offset/nextOffset to get the rest)

tools.title: Look up a word

tools.name: get_word_occurrences
tools.description: Lists every verse that contains a Strong's number (Hebrew Tanakh, Greek New Testament and Septuagint), in Bible order with the verse text, plus the count per book. Covers every form of the word; optionally limited to one book. 10 verses per page by default (limit 1-25, and nextOffset continues). Use when the user asks where a particular Hebrew or Greek word occurs.

strongs.description: a Strong's number such as H2617 (Hebrew) or G26 (Greek)

book.description: restrict to one book code or name, e.g. PSA or Psalms

limit.description: how many results to return (1-25, default 10)

offset.description: how many results to skip; the previous answer's nextOffset is where its page ended

max_chars.description: optional: cap the answer at about this many characters (lists are shortened and marked truncated; use offset/nextOffset to get the rest)

tools.title: Every verse a word is in

annotations.title: Every verse a word is in

tools.name: get_related_passages
tools.description: Returns the verses connected to one verse, grouped by kind: voted cross-references, quotations in either direction between books, curated parallel passages, and similar wording. Use when the user asks what passages are related to one verse.

max_chars.description: optional: cap the answer at about this many characters (lists are shortened and marked truncated; use offset/nextOffset to get the rest)

tools.title: Related passages

tools.name: get_cross_references
tools.description: Returns the voted cross-references (OpenBible.info) of one verse, each with its reference and link; the first few also carry their English text. 12 by default (limit 1-30). Use when the user asks for the cross-references of one verse.

limit.description: how many results to return (1-30, default 12)

max_chars.description: optional: cap the answer at about this many characters (lists are shortened and marked truncated; use offset/nextOffset to get the rest)

tools.title: Cross-references

tools.name: get_book_connections
tools.description: Returns the chapters a book, or one chapter, is most connected to elsewhere in the Bible: chapter pairs joined by at least two verse-level cross-references (OpenBible.info), most-linked first, each with its link count and a link. 15 by default (limit 1-40). Use when the user asks which chapters a book or chapter is most connected to.

limit.description: how many results to return (1-40, default 15)

max_chars.description: optional: cap the answer at about this many characters (lists are shortened and marked truncated; use offset/nextOffset to get the rest)

tools.title: Connections between books

tools.name: list_books
tools.description: Returns every book with its code, chapter count, the editions it exists in and its URL, and the list of editions. The whole list comes back in one piece. Use when the user asks what books, editions or book codes are available.

max_chars.description: optional: cap the answer at about this many characters (lists are shortened and marked truncated; use offset/nextOffset to get the rest)

tools.title: List the books

tools.name: list_songs
tools.description: Returns the songs and prayers inside Scripture (the Song of the Sea, Hannah's prayer, the Magnificat…), each with its name, Hebrew title, kind (victory, prophetic, thanksgiving, boast, prayer, work song, blessing, lament or hymn), passage reference and link. kind narrows the list; otherwise the whole list comes back in one piece. Use when the user asks which songs and prayers appear inside Scripture, such as the Song of the Sea or the Magnificat.

kind.description: kind of song or prayer, e.g. victory, lament, prayer, blessing, hymn, thanksgiving

max_chars.description: optional: cap the answer at about this many characters (lists are shortened and marked truncated; use offset/nextOffset to get the rest)

tools.title: Songs and prayers in Scripture

tools.name: list_questions
tools.description: Returns pairs of passages in which a question asked in one place is answered in another (e.g. 'what is man?' in Job and Psalm 8). Each pair has its theme, the asking and answering passages, and a note. theme (god, man, suffering, sin, death, time, wisdom, worship, messiah) or contains narrows the list; unfiltered, every pair comes back in one large piece. Use when the user asks about a question in one passage that another passage answers.

theme.description: theme id: god, man, suffering, sin, death, time, wisdom, worship or messiah

contains.description: only questions whose text contains this word

max_chars.description: optional: cap the answer at about this many characters (lists are shortened and marked truncated; use offset/nextOffset to get the rest)

tools.title: Questions and their answers

tools.name: get_targum_connections
tools.description: Returns the curated list of places where the Targumim (the Aramaic translations of the Torah and Isaiah) and the New Testament share an idea, phrase or contrast. Each entry has a title, whether it is a shared idea or a contrast, the Targum passages, the New Testament passages, and a note saying what is and is not claimed. The whole list comes back in one piece; it takes no filter. Use when the user asks where Targum wording and the New Testament overlap.

max_chars.description: optional: cap the answer at about this many characters (lists are shortened and marked truncated; use offset/nextOffset to get the rest)

tools.title: Targum connections

tools.name: get_septuagint_connections
tools.description: Returns the curated places where a Hebrew term or idea is carried through the Greek Old Testament (the Septuagint) into the New Testament. Each entry has a title, its kind (a Greek word traced back to its Hebrew term, an idea the Greek says more openly than the Masoretic Hebrew, or a passage from a book found only in Greek), the Hebrew, Greek (Septuagint numbering) and New Testament passages, Strong's pairs for word entries, and a note saying what is and is not claimed. kind (idea, word, only), topic (lord, messiah, covenant, life) or contains narrows the list; unfiltered, every entry comes back in one large piece. Use when the user asks how a New Testament Greek word or idea traces back through the Septuagint to the Hebrew canon.

kind.description: idea (the Greek says it more openly), word (a Greek word traced back) or only (a book found only in Greek)

contains.description: only entries whose title or note contains this text

max_chars.description: optional: cap the answer at about this many characters (lists are shortened and marked truncated; use offset/nextOffset to get the rest)

tools.title: Hebrew, Greek and New Testament links

annotations.title: Hebrew, Greek and New Testament links

tools.name: get_parashah
tools.description: Returns a weekly Torah portion: its name, Hebrew name, meaning and Shabbat date, with its Torah, Haftarah and Besorah (New Testament) readings and links, on the Diaspora calendar. Give a name ('Toledot'), a date (YYYY-MM-DD) for the portion read on the Shabbat on or after it, or list=true for every portion; with none, this week's. Use when the user asks about a weekly Torah portion, its Haftarah or its New Testament reading.

date.description: a date as YYYY-MM-DD; gives the portion read on the Shabbat on or after it

max_chars.description: optional: cap the answer at about this many characters (lists are shortened and marked truncated; use offset/nextOffset to get the rest)

tools.title: Weekly Torah portion

tools.name: get_guide
tools.description: Returns a plain-text guide to Besorah's texts and conventions: the editions, the Hebrew-based verse numbering, Strong's ids (H… Hebrew, G… Greek), book codes, and what each study tool returns. Use when the user asks how the texts, numbering and ids work.

max_chars.description: optional: cap the answer at about this many characters (lists are shortened and marked truncated; use offset/nextOffset to get the rest)

tools.title: Guide to the texts and tools

annotations.title: Guide to the texts and tools

tools.name: query_words
tools.description: Finds every word by grammar and/or Strong's number, within a book or testament — e.g. all Qal imperatives of H1285 in the Prophets, every aorist passive participle in Paul, every Hiphil verb in Isaiah. grammar takes the words of the parsing (Qal, Hiphil, imperative, participle, feminine, plural, aorist, passive, genitive, 3rd…); all must be on the same word. Hebrew by default for H ids and Tanakh books, Greek for G ids and the New Testament; edition=septuagint for the Septuagint. Returns the matching words with their verses and a count per book, 10 per page by default (limit 1-25, and nextOffset continues). Use when the user asks for words by grammatical form, such as every Qal imperative or aorist passive participle.

book.description: restrict to one book, e.g. Isaiah

limit.description: how many results to return (1-25, default 10)

offset.description: how many results to skip; the previous answer's nextOffset is where its page ended

max_chars.description: optional: cap the answer at about this many characters (lists are shortened and marked truncated; use offset/nextOffset to get the rest)

tools.title: Find words by grammar

tools.name: get_collocations
tools.description: Returns the words that keep company with a Hebrew or Greek word: those that appear in the same verse more often than chance predicts (log-likelihood), strongest first, 15 by default (limit 1-25). Pass strongs (H430) or a word ('shepherd'). Pass with=<Strong's id> to read the verses where two words meet. corpus: he, nt or lxx. Use when the user asks which words commonly appear alongside a given Hebrew or Greek word.

with.description: a second Strong's id, to see the verses with both

corpus.description: he (Hebrew Bible), nt (Greek New Testament) or lxx (Septuagint)

limit.description: how many results to return (1-25, default 15)

max_chars.description: optional: cap the answer at about this many characters (lists are shortened and marked truncated; use offset/nextOffset to get the rest)

tools.title: Words that keep company

tools.name: get_vocabulary
tools.description: Returns a book's vocabulary. view=summary (default) gives its size, distinct words, hapax legomena (words used once in the whole text), words found only in that book, and its most frequent and most characteristic words; view=hapax, unique or words lists those words (25 per page by default, limit 1-100, and nextOffset continues). Use when the user asks about one book's vocabulary, rare words or words unique to it.

limit.description: how many results to return (1-100, default 25)

offset.description: how many results to skip; the previous answer's nextOffset is where its page ended

max_chars.description: optional: cap the answer at about this many characters (lists are shortened and marked truncated; use offset/nextOffset to get the rest)

tools.title: A book's vocabulary

tools.name: compare_books
tools.description: Compares two books' vocabularies: the word counts of each, how many words they share, the rare words they share (most of whose uses are in these two books), and the words only one uses, 15 of each by default (limit 1-40). Same language only: two Hebrew books, two Greek ones, or a Septuagint book (editionA: septuagint) against a New Testament book. Use when the user asks how the vocabularies of two books compare.

editionA.description: edition of the first book, e.g. septuagint

editionB.description: edition of the second book, e.g. hebrew-nt

limit.description: how many results to return (1-40, default 15)

max_chars.description: optional: cap the answer at about this many characters (lists are shortened and marked truncated; use offset/nextOffset to get the rest)

tools.title: Compare two books' vocabulary

tools.name: get_context
tools.description: Returns a verse in its setting in one call: the verses before and after (2 each by default, 0-8), the verse itself, or up to 5, word by word, and its cross-references, quotations and parallels. Combines several lookups into one answer. Use when the user asks what surrounds a verse, with its neighbouring verses and connections.

edition.description: which text, e.g. septuagint, onkelos, pseudo-jonathan, jonathan, hebrew-nt, hebrew or greek

max_chars.description: optional: cap the answer at about this many characters (lists are shortened and marked truncated; use offset/nextOffset to get the rest)

tools.title: A verse in its setting

tools.name: trace_theme
tools.description: Follows a passage's connections outward — voted cross-references plus quotations and parallels between books — one to three steps (depth, default 2), and returns the most strongly connected verses (20 by default, limit 1-40) with their text, hops from the start, strength (it grows with the number of short paths that reach the verse) and how each was reached. Example: the connections of Passover outward from Exodus 12. Use when the user asks to follow a theme or passage outward through the Bible.

reference.description: a verse, short range or chapter

follow.description: both, xref (cross-references only) or quotes (quotations and parallels only)

limit.description: how many results to return (1-40, default 20)

max_chars.description: optional: cap the answer at about this many characters (lists are shortened and marked truncated; use offset/nextOffset to get the rest)

tools.title: Trace a theme

tools.name: compare_witnesses
tools.description: Returns one verse across the texts side by side: Hebrew, the Septuagint (matched by the app's verse tables, even where numbered differently), the Targumim, and the Greek and Hebrew New Testament, with the quotations that join them and the Greek words a New Testament quotation and the Septuagint do and do not share. Use when the user asks how one verse reads in the Hebrew, Septuagint, Targum and New Testament.

max_chars.description: optional: cap the answer at about this many characters (lists are shortened and marked truncated; use offset/nextOffset to get the rest)

tools.title: Compare the texts of a verse

annotations.title: Compare the texts of a verse

tools.name: get_quotations
tools.description: Returns where the New Testament quotes the Old, in either direction: give a New Testament book, chapter or verse for the Old Testament passages it quotes, or an Old Testament one for the New Testament passages that quote it. Each result carries both English texts and a link; 15 per page by default (limit 1-40, and nextOffset continues). Use when the user asks where the New Testament quotes the Old Testament, or the reverse.

limit.description: how many results to return (1-40, default 15)

offset.description: how many results to skip; the previous answer's nextOffset is where its page ended

max_chars.description: optional: cap the answer at about this many characters (lists are shortened and marked truncated; use offset/nextOffset to get the rest)
